codebase-question.name: Codebase Question
codebase-question.description: Research the codebase thoroughly to answer the user's question. Read relevant files, trace code paths, and check git history as needed to build a complete understanding. Report your findings inline in the conversation — do not create files, PRs, or branches. Once you have answered the question with sufficient depth and evidence, stop and wait in `needs_input` state. Then archive or stop according to who asked. If a human invoked this session directly, do NOT archive yourself — a human-asked question is one of the sanctioned reasons a session stays in `needs_input` rather than self-archiving, and the user reviews your answer on the Zimmer homepage and archives the session themselves. If a parent session spawned you to research something on its behalf, report your answer back to that parent and archive yourself; there is no human waiting on this session. If the user asks follow-up questions, answer them.

open-reviewed-green-pr.name: Open Reviewed Green PR
open-reviewed-green-pr.description: Unmerged PR is open, CI is confirmed green (use the wait-for-CI skill to block until CI passes or fails), and an independent fresh-eyes review of the PR has been performed and all of its feedback addressed (use wait-for-CI again after any fixes). Run that review through your runtime's in-process review path — the /code-review skill, Claude Code's native Task/Agent subagent, or Codex's native spawn_agent subagent — and do NOT spin up a separate Zimmer session solely to review your own PR (reserve start_session for genuinely independent downstream work). Open and finalize the PR through the `open-pr` skill — it commits your changes, pushes the feature branch, opens (or updates) the PR, self-reviews, and runs its terminal steps; do not hand-roll your own commit/push/PR sequence when that skill is available. Ensure the PR title/description accurately reflects the final implementation. The PR description MUST include a '## Verification' section with checked boxes documenting how you closed the loop (CI green, tests added/passing, self-review done) AND proof that the change works (screenshots for UI changes, e2e test results for logic changes, external confirmation for side effects). For UI changes, follow the screenshot capture-upload-embed procedure in GIT_WORKFLOW.md. Do NOT use unchecked checkboxes or a 'Test plan' with aspirational TODOs — every verification item must be completed before the PR is opened. Once the PR is open, CI is green, and self-review + fresh-eyes review are complete, apply the `ready to merge` label — the `open-pr` skill's terminal step does this. Applying the `ready to merge` label does NOT merge the PR and does NOT claim a human has reviewed it — it is the agent's own claim that self-review, fresh-eyes review, and green CI are complete. It is fully compatible with leaving the PR unmerged — you never merge your own PR; a goal that says 'do not merge / leave it for the human' is not a reason to skip the label. Then report the PR URL and a summary of what changed, and hold the work rather than ending it: do NOT archive yourself yet, and do NOT merge the PR. This session holds the work's context, so it is the session a human comes back to while the PR's disposition is unsettled. For HOW to come to rest, follow the `open-pr` skill's terminal steps instead of parking straight away — a PR merely waiting for the merge gate to rate it is a machine wait, so the skill has you schedule a bounded self-wake and end the turn in `waiting`, then on each wake make one PR-state check and take exactly one row of the skill's decision table: merged, or closed unmerged, means archive; a fresh merge-gate HELD verdict, a label that has come off, a spent wake budget, or a PR state you could not read means come to rest in needs_input; a PR still open and unrated means sleep again. Sleeping and stopping are the same holding pattern — same session, same context, same PR — minus the homepage action-queue slot for the interval in which nothing yet needs a human. If the `open-pr` skill is not available to you — another runtime, a repo that does not ship it, or no self-session MCP server to schedule a wake with — then come to rest in needs_input holding the PR instead; that is the fallback, not a failure. Either way you do not have to watch it. Zimmer's pull-request poller sends this session a message when the PR merges, and THAT MESSAGE IS YOUR SIGNAL TO ARCHIVE — at that point the work is done, nothing is left for a human, and you should archive yourself immediately rather than waiting to be told twice. If a merge gate holds the PR for human review instead, no message comes until a human merges it — and coming to rest in needs_input is exactly right there, because that human is what the queue is for: a PR the gate has held is a human handoff, not a machine wait. Archive early in three cases: the PR was closed without merging, every PR you opened has reached a terminal state, or Zimmer never recorded a PR URL for this session. That last one matters: the poller only knows about PRs it saw you open, so a PR created by a route it does not recognise is invisible to it and no message can ever reach you — check with get_session, and if there is no recorded URL, report the PR URL in your final message and archive instead of waiting forever. What you must NOT do is treat this session as a permanent todo item for a PR that has already landed — a session still sitting in needs_input, or still sleeping on a self-wake, after its PR merged is the failure this instruction exists to prevent.
